en.title: Tokyo stays: Shinagawa, Osaki, Gotanda
en.cardDesc: Three spots on the Yamanote Line, each with a different neighborhood feel.
en.html:
Tokyo stays: Shinagawa, Osaki, Gotanda

Source: Merry Journey

Shinagawa（品川）

The easiest station for Haneda — Keikyu takes about 15–20 minutes. Stay at 品川王子大飯店 — about two minutes from the station, Tokyo Tower from the high floors, pool / bowling / cinema on site.

Next door is Maxell Aqua Park, a compact aquarium with dolphin shows (the first four rows get splashed).

Osaki（大崎）

One stop down the Yamanote, plus the Rinkai Line straight to Odaiba — more of a lived-in Tokyo feel. New Otani Inn Tokyo connects to the station under cover, with rooms wider than a typical business hotel. Behind it, OAKI New City has a large supermarket (wagyu, prepared food), Daiso, and plenty to eat.

Gotanda（五反田）

Transfer to the Toei Asakusa Line for Skytree, Ginza, Nihonbashi; some trains run through to Narita. 東急 Stay 五反田 is under 10 seconds from exit A6, with a washer and microwave — useful for longer stays. A one-minute walk to a five-floor Don Quijote.

en.title: Five beef noodle shops in Hsinchu
en.cardDesc: One bowl each at Chenghuang Temple, NTHU, Guangfu Road, Zhongzheng Road, and Zhubei — the map is what shows the distance.
en.html:
Five beef noodle shops in Hsinchu

Hsinchu beef noodle is not one street competing with itself — it is five points. Chenghuang Temple, NTHU, Guangfu Road, Zhongzheng Road, and Zhubei each get a bowl; the map is what shows the distance. All five were still open in 2026. Hours and closing days follow the shops; no prices here.

九添福牛肉麵館

九添福牛肉麵館 is at No. 436, Xida Road, North District, a few minutes' walk from 城隍廟. Still on the 2026 Bib Gourmand list. Both red-braised and clear broth; generous meat. Parking around the temple is hard — treat the shop as the pin.

璽子牛肉麵

璽子牛肉麵 main shop is at No. 31, Bo'ai Street, East District, on the municipal zoo / NTHU side. Clear broth, tendon with bite. The jinbing often sells out. Closed Tuesdays; lunch and dinner only. Zhubei and Xiangshan have branches; this piece pins the main shop.

成都老鍋牛肉麵

成都老鍋牛肉麵 is at No. 126, Sec. 2, Guangfu Road, East District — the Hsinchu Science Park / NTHU after-work axis. Sichuan-leaning but not pure heat; the bone broth cooks longer. Closed Wednesdays. Same stretch as 璽子 on Bo'ai Street, but too far to walk as one meal. Treat them as two pins.

臻穎牛肉麵食館

臻穎牛肉麵食館 is at No. 366, Zhongzheng Road, near the Air Force Hospital and Big City. Moved from Minsheng Road in 2025. Thirty-plus years of juancun taste. The Five Blessings bowl puts tendon, tendon core, pork belly, tripe, and tendon in one bowl. Closed Mondays; cars are hard to park nearby.

文化城牛肉麵

文化城牛肉麵 jumps to No. 486, Guangming 1st Road, Zhubei — not the same map scale as the four in the city. Large cuts, many small plates; iced tea refills for dine-in. Closed Thursdays. The pig's trotter often sells out; come early if you want it on the side.

Do not try all five in one day. Pick one bowl as this visit's anchor, then start the next from the other side of the map.

en.title: Yangmingshan: one night, two days on foot
en.cardDesc: Tienlai as the base. Qixing from Xiaoyoukeng; the fish trail uphill the next day.
en.html:
Yangmingshan: one night, two days on foot

Split a holiday from a workout and the weekend becomes two jobs: one day sleeping in the car, one day forcing a climb. This time we flipped it — book 陽明山天籟渡假酒店 as the base, climb 七星山 on Saturday, and on Sunday climb the fish trail from 上磺溪 toward 擎天崗, both days from the same bed.

Why Tienlai

This is the seaward side of Yangmingshan, not the Beitou strip. 天籟 is in Jinshan. After enough Qixing sulfur on the mountain, the nose is already dull in the lobby. The lower end of the north fish trail is on this side — Sunday you can start at the foot and climb up, then back to the bed, without stuffing yourself back into the city. Soak the legs and stop.

Saturday｜Qixing

Park at 小油坑 and start the climb to 七星山主峰 from there. Short, steep stone steps; fumaroles hiss beside you; sulfur works into the throat. The legs complain before the lungs. Wind on the summit dries the sweat; only wind left in the ears. Below: white smoke and ridgeline, not a view staged for anyone. Sit a while, then the same way down. Legs still shaking back at Tienlai; the water is the temperature that matches the day.

Sunday｜north fish trail, uphill

Day two is not another Qixing. Walk the fish trail — Jinbaoli Road, the old route that carried fish over the mountain. This day we climb: start at 上磺溪, through 憨丙厝地 (you can stop by the stone house and catch your breath — travelers used to mend straw sandals here), then on toward 金包里城門 / Qingtiangang. Uneven stone steps underfoot, shade in stretches; where the soles pick up wet soil, the stride shortens on its own. This day is a climb, not a slide from the gate down toward Xiahuangxi.

We walked it then. Check the notices before you start at Shanghuangxi; if it is closed, do not treat this route as current.

Map order: Tienlai → Xiaoyoukeng / Qixing → Shanghuangxi → Hanbingcuodi → the gate (uphill) → back to Tienlai. Two days, one sleeping coordinate.

Still to write: other north-Taiwan “one night + two days on foot,” bikes, the coast, living-water lake days off — pin those next. First piece in the resort-fitness series.

en.title: Tokyo tabletop market: how to stay in Makuhari, which day to recover (Autumn 2026)
en.cardDesc: Pin the bed and recovery first; after two hall days, leave another day for the legs.
en.html:
Tokyo tabletop market: how to stay in Makuhari, which day to recover (Autumn 2026)

Not gone yet. For October I want to park a holiday on Tokyo's tabletop-game market — Japanese usually writes ゲームマーケット / Game Market. Not a video-game expo: you playtest and buy new titles. Both days are standing playtests; the bag only gets heavier. What I want clear is how close the bed is to the hall, and which day I soak the legs or take the sea wind.

Makuhari — do not commute from Shinjuku

幕張メッセ sits against 海浜幕張. The picture I want: bags back in the room, then into the hall empty-handed. If the fair means a Shinjuku run every night, the legs will fail before the wallet. 2026/10/17–18; details on gamemarket.jp. Booth maps are only accurate at the door; this piece does not draw them.

Check in first

Find a bed on the Kaihin-Makuhari side. 10/16 can be the arrival: land in Tokyo, check in, deal with jet lag and luggage, then walk in Saturday and Sunday. Shop names wait until that year's rooms; do not sleep cheap an hour away.

Two days in the hall, leave another day for the legs

The hall is only Saturday and Sunday. The trip can be: one day land and check in, two days playtesting inside メッセ, then a full day off the floor, last day home. That day is not for packing in sights — the legs already stood two days; stuffing an outlet or a city tour only makes them worse the next morning. Better the waterfront, a soak, or staying in the room, so the legs can come back.

Sea wind

幕張海浜公園. When the hall lights and voices are still in the ears, go look at the horizon. Walk a loop or ride a short stretch; stop when the wind is enough.

Hot water

幕張温泉 湯楽の里 is more on-target than a mall. After two days standing, what you want is to get in the water. Over by JFA Yume Field; how to get there and how much, check the official site before you go.

One dinner outside the hall is enough, around the station. Three things on the map: メッセ, a bed you can get back to, the park or the bath. Tickets and hours follow the official site.

en.title: A walking elephant in the Nantes shipyard
en.cardDesc: Not been yet. The mechanical elephant, the river rings, the grey crane.
en.html:
A walking elephant in the Nantes shipyard

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. Nantes sits on the west of France, toward the Atlantic; the high-speed train from Paris is a little over two hours. On the river island an old shipyard became a mechanical-art park — not a zoo. I want to go for the mechanical elephant that lifts its legs and walks: Les Machines de l'Île (Machines of the Isle of Nantes). Check the downtime calendar before you leave.

Les Machines de l'Île

The park is at the west end of Île de Nantes, in the Loire, at Parc des Chantiers. The headline is the Grand Éléphant: about twelve metres high, about forty-eight tonnes, wood and steel, ears that move, a trunk that mists water, walking slowly through the park. Standing in the park you can watch it pass for free; a Voyage ticket is what lets you climb on for about thirty minutes, around forty or fifty people at a time, and from the back you can see how the joints lift the legs. Departures are limited; in high season you usually book online first.

What the elephant walks on

Electricity — battery / hybrid traction; the legs and joints are lifted mainly by hydraulics and pneumatics, not petrol. It walks slowly. After the 2018 hybrid change it is quieter. A driver steers. Details: lesmachines-nantes.fr／Grand Éléphant.

The gallery and the marine carousel

The other two blocks are separate tickets. Galerie des Machines is a living machine hall: spiders, insects, birds and other large mechanical creatures, about an hour, with operators who talk and make the machines move. Carrousel des Mondes Marins (Marine Worlds Carousel) is a three-storey sea carousel, about forty-five minutes; every level has sit-on, moving marine machines — not the little wooden horses of a fairground. The park itself is free to walk. The heron tree they used to advertise (Arbre aux Hérons) was cancelled; only prototype branches remain on site, so do not expect the whole tree from old posters.

When you cannot ride the elephant

The Grand Éléphant does no Voyage from 2026/11/2–2027/2/28 (follow lesmachines-nantes.fr/horaires). The Machines stay open in that window; only the elephant ride is crossed out. The marine carousel has a separate maintenance window 2026/9/21–25; check the same page again before you go.

West along the river

After the Machines I still want to walk west along the river to Quai des Antilles. Les Anneaux is a string of rings standing on the bank; at dusk you want to walk around them. Hangar à Bananes sits on the quay; further on is the grey Grue Titan grise — do not mix it up with the yellow crane inside the park. The north-bank Mémorial de l'abolition is across a bridge, not a few more steps along the same shore.

How other people wrote it

These are other people's trip notes / reports online, not a record of my being there — only for the picture. Do not treat old ticket prices and timetables as current; follow the official site: Room7B01〈Les Machines〉 (Traditional Chinese, on-site detail); RFI〈南特機械島〉 (Traditional Chinese; 2016, atmosphere only); One Small Bag (English, elephant / Galerie / carousel written separately); Petit Futé visit (French).

The picture I want: the west coast of France, shipyard ground, a twelve-metre mechanical elephant, the gallery and a three-level marine carousel, rings and a grey crane on the riverbank. Tickets, downtime, bridges and trams — check the official site again before you go.

en.title: Fulong: one night, bike Old Caoling
en.cardDesc: Want to go. Overnight at Fullon, bike Old Caoling; soak at the beach.
en.html:
Fulong: one night, bike Old Caoling

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. The Yangmingshan piece pinned holiday and workout to the same bed, and said bikes and the coast were still to write. This time I want to park the holiday in Fulong — book 福容 for one night, then the next day pick up a bike at 福隆車站 and ride into 舊草嶺隧道, both days starting from the same sandspit.

Why Fullon

福容大飯店福隆 sits against the 浴場 and the sandspit — the overnight pole on this map. After the ride or the swim, what you want is to walk back to the room and soak the legs in the ocean hot spring, not drive back into the city. Check fullon-hotels before you go.

The station as hub

福隆車站 is where the bento and the station-front bike rentals sit on top of each other. Bikes leave from here; the tunnel starts counting from here. The pin is approximate — check the rental stall again when you arrive.

Old Caoling: north mouth to south mouth

The ride I want is Old Caoling, not a highway loop. The 北口 is on the Fulong side; the tourism bureau writes 制天險. The 南口 is the Shicheng end, 白雲飛處. Cool inside the tunnel; turn around after the south mouth. The south-mouth pin is a track approximation, not a single official page.

River inside, sea outside

福隆遊客中心 and the 海水浴場 sit on the same side: inner river, outer sea, sand for a swim. The sea-swim season is about 5/1–10/20, lifeguards until 17:00. Details on the Fullon beach page.

Short ridge to the west

I still want to walk west along the sand to 龍門吊橋 — the stretch that joins Longmen to Yanliao. Short, windy. Not the main line; the edge after the tunnel.

Map order: Fullon → station / rental → north mouth → south mouth (and back) → visitor centre / beach → Longmen Bridge → back to Fullon. Two days, one sleeping coordinate.

Resort-fitness series: after two days on foot in Yangmingshan, this piece is the bike and the coast. Still to write: a living-water lake day off — pin that next.

en.title: Akiyoshido: seventeen degrees underground, elevator up to the plateau
en.cardDesc: Not been yet. Seventeen degrees underground, Hundred Dishes, Golden Pillar, elevator to the plateau.
en.html:
Akiyoshido: seventeen degrees underground, elevator up to the plateau

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. Akiyoshido（あきよしどう） sits on the west of Honshu, in Yamaguchi — about a hundred metres under Mine City's Akiyoshidai Quasi-National Park, a national natural monument. Official pages often say one of the largest; the cave system is Japan's second-longest. I want to go to walk the underground at about seventeen degrees first, then take the elevator up onto the limestone plateau and match the formations to the surface: 秋芳洞正面入口. Do not stuff Shimonoseki, Motonosumi, and Hagi into the same day.

In through the main entrance

The tourist main line starts at the front entrance, about one paved kilometre; the cave stays about seventeen degrees year-round, damp and slippery — trainers and a light jacket. On the way you pass 百枚皿 (travertine terraces stacked like rice paddies) and 黃金柱（黄金柱）. Exact spots inside the cave only line up once you are in; this map starts from the front entrance. From April 2026 tickets and the ticket window changed; check the Japanese official site before you leave (the Traditional Chinese page may be old).

The adventure course is not a caving tour

Beside the main line there is an 冒險コース: a little extra money, a rented torch, a side branch of about ten to fifteen minutes; it closes when the water rises. Details on the official site. This is not a caving tour. If the legs are not enough, just walk the paved kilometre.

Elevator up to the plateau

Midway you can take the elevator to the surface and walk to カルスト展望台 (the limestone-plateau lookout). One ticket lets you re-enter the cave — see the formations below, then grassland and sinkholes above. Choosing the front entrance or the elevator entrance is choosing whether to keep a stretch of energy for the plateau.

How to get there, do not stuff the day

JR Shin-Yamaguchi, then the Bocho Bus to 「秋芳洞」, about forty to forty-five minutes — that is the current main line. The JR Mine Line is still fully suspended; do not treat the train as running. Sections are replacement buses; leave extra time for the connection. By car, get off near Akiyoshidai IC. Taishodo, Shimonoseki / Tsunoshima / Motonosumi, and Hagi / Tsuwano are other days.

The picture I want: west Honshu, seventeen degrees under Mine, Hundred Dishes and the Golden Pillar, an optional torch side-branch, elevator up to the Akiyoshidai grassland. Check karusuto.com／秋芳洞 before you leave.
